title: Spark History Server performance improvement: Snapshot-based loading (Preview)
summary: Microsoft describes a rework of the Fabric Spark History Server's log-loading path, moving from an all-at-once event-log parse to an incremental, snapshot-based read so large Spark UIs open far faster.
audience: Data engineers and platform admins who debug Spark jobs in Fabric via the History Server UI, especially teams running large-scale batch or long-running streaming workloads.
why_it_matters: History Server load time has been a real operational bottleneck for enterprise-scale Spark jobs; this change also lifts a prior restriction on event-log compression/rolling, which affects how teams configure long-running streaming jobs.
takeaways: The Spark History Server historically had to fully parse an application's entire event log before rendering, which could take up to an hour or fail outright on very large jobs.
A new preview snapshot-based loading mode reads metrics and logs incrementally, showing an initial batch quickly and fetching further detail on demand.
This same release also removes a prior restriction on event log compression and rolling for long-running/streaming jobs.
The feature is explicitly labeled Preview, not GA.

claims.text: The Fabric Spark History Server previously required fully parsing and rendering an application's entire event log before its UI would load, which made this a bottleneck for large workloads.

For enterprise-scale Spark applications with hundreds of thousands of tasks or event logs over 10 GB, or for long-running Spark Streaming jobs, History Server load time could reach roughly an hour, and in some cases loading failed entirely.

In preview, the Fabric Spark History Server can load execution metrics and logs incrementally via a snapshot-based approach instead of processing the full event log up front, surfacing an initial batch of data quickly and pulling further detail on demand.
With snapshot-based loading, applications that previously took up to roughly an hour to open in the History Server can instead render in seconds to minutes.

This release also lifts a prior restriction that had blocked enabling the spark.eventLog.compress and spark.eventLog.rolling.enabled properties, which previously caused the History Server to fail to render when set.
Event log compression and log rolling can now be enabled for Spark Streaming and other long-running applications while the History Server continues to render correctly.
